Painting and plastering helpers stage and deliver materials and tools for painting, paperhanging, plastering or stucco crews. They check labels and counts, protect assigned surfaces and clean work areas. Ask the site lead about ventilation, protective controls, tools and work at height.

The exact occupation 47-3014 assists painters, paperhangers, plasterers or stucco masons with less-skilled tasks, delivering tools and materials and cleaning. Its current 11 tasks comprise 7 Core and 4 Supplemental tasks. Cleaning 82, supplying 79, masking 72, sanding 69, erecting scaffolding 61, assisting 55, and filling cracks 55 are Core; mixing plaster 41 and paint-stripping tank tasks 33 / 33 / 31 are Supplemental and are not shared duties of every position. The original activity ratings—inspection 80, information 79, physical activity 78, control 77 and communication 76—are listed by O*NET. For the exact U.S. BLS occupation 47-3014, typical entry requirements are no formal educational credential, no related work experience, and short-term on-the-job training. O*NET's new-hire figures of 68% below high school, 26% high school and 4% postsecondary certificate are surveyed requirements, not Chinese entry requirements or the educational composition of all workers. O*NET occupational interest scores are R 92, C 41, S 24, A 13, I 2, E 6.  Current work style scores of dependability 66, cooperation 52, attention to detail 46 and cautiousness 41 describe the occupation and do not predict individual performance.

Standards and quality boundaries | This page involves three types of requirements. First, technical quality: mixing, surface preparation, sanding, masking, painting or plastering, and cleaning must follow procedures and current acceptance standards, with materials and work records maintained. Second, safety and occupational health: solvents, paints, chemicals, ventilation, fire prevention, scaffolding, heights, open edges, dust and personal protection must meet construction safety and occupational health requirements. Third, environmental protection and orderly construction: disposal of solvent and paint residues, waste, dust and noise must meet environmental protection and orderly construction requirements. All three are subject to currently effective versions and the requirements of competent authorities and the enterprise.

Records and collaboration | If safeguards fail, a hazard is unclear or a request exceeds the assignment, stop, step clear and tell the site lead. Keep original readings and times within your role. Designated staff decide on isolation, response and restart.

Boundary conclusion | This page covers O*NET 47-3014.00, Helpers--Painters, Paperhangers, Plasterers, and Stucco Masons. Its central distinction from neighboring roles is the objects of work, outputs and level of authorization. It deals with paint, solvents, mortar, putty, substrates, scaffolding and on-site assistance. Outputs are assistance completed according to procedures—materials, mixing, surface preparation, masking, application and cleaning—and traceable materials and work records. Work is completed through materials, tools and site coordination skills within skilled workers' instructions and job authorization, with responsibility for work safety, process quality and site order. Construction and maintenance painters, plasterers, stucco masons, paperhangers and drywall installers produce work in their own specialties, with different responsibility and authorization levels.

Core principle of neighboring roles | Most related and neighboring roles aim to complete painting, plastering, paperhanging or finishing to specified quality within procedural and safety requirements, with records retained. Differences concern the objects of work, outputs and authorization levels: some focus on independent application and forming, while others focus on on-site assistance, materials and cleaning.

Core purpose of this occupation | Work with paint, solvents, mortar, putty, substrates and procedures within skilled workers' instructions, safety requirements and authorization: materials, supplying and mixing; surface preparation, sanding and filling cracks; masking and protection; application assistance; and cleaning, curing and recording. Outputs are assistance that meets procedural requirements and traceable records.

Main work objects and bases of neighboring roles | Construction and maintenance painters follow painting procedures and coating requirements; plasterers and stucco masons follow plastering and stucco procedures; paperhangers follow wallpaper and paperhanging procedures; drywall and ceiling tile installers follow light-gauge steel framing and panel installation procedures; construction laborers follow general construction and operating procedures. Most focus on independent application and forming, unlike this occupation's on-site assistance.

Main work objects and bases of this occupation | Work with the work location and drawing number, substrate material and condition, paint or mortar, putty and masking material specifications, mixing and stirring, surface preparation, sanding and dust removal, masking and protection, scaffolding and ventilation, and cleaning and curing requirements. Provide assistance and make judgments according to procedures, current acceptance standards, and construction safety and occupational health requirements.

Occupational profile | Helpers stage materials and tools, assist with masking or surface preparation, and clean work areas as assigned. Exposure to sanding dust, material odors, noise, heights or cramped areas depends on the process, materials, equipment and site. Ask about the actual work area, safeguards, supervision and which equipment you can use. For scaffold, spray or other tasks subject to special rules, check the requirements for training, qualifications and authorization.

Core processes of neighboring roles | Construction and maintenance painters focus on applying and forming paint finishes; plasterers and stucco masons focus on plaster and stucco application; paperhangers focus on cutting and hanging wallpaper; drywall installers focus on framing and panel installation; this occupation focuses on assistance with materials, mixing, surface preparation, masking and cleaning.

Core process of this occupation | Receive assignments and check substrates; prepare materials, mixes and protection; prepare surfaces, sand and remove dust; apply masking and protective coverings; assist with painting, plastering or paperhanging; and clean, cure, restore, record and hand over. Every step must follow procedures and skilled workers' instructions and be open to review by skilled workers, quality inspectors and safety personnel.

Main outputs of neighboring roles | Construction and maintenance painters produce coatings, finishes and acceptance records; plasterers and stucco masons produce plaster surfaces, finishes and acceptance records; paperhangers produce papered surfaces and acceptance records; drywall installers produce partitions, suspended ceilings and installation records. These differ from this occupation's assistance and materials and work records.

Main outputs of this occupation | Assistance completed according to procedures: mixed paint, mortar and putty; prepared, sanded and dust-free substrates; installed masking and protection; assistance with painting, plastering or paperhanging; and cleaned and restored sites. Outputs also include materials, work and inspection records; quantities, leftover materials and rework records; abnormalities and outstanding items; and traceable shift and handover records.

Responsibility in neighboring roles | Responsibility in related and neighboring roles is usually defined by the employer and its construction, safety and quality systems, primarily concerning finish quality, personal safety, schedules, fire prevention and environmental protection.

Workers in this occupation are responsible for their own mixing, surface preparation, sanding, masking, cleaning and records, and for assistance completed according to procedures and safety requirements. Matters involving scaffold erection or dismantling, chemicals and fire prevention, heights and open edges, or major quality and safety issues must be referred to the appropriate roles or organizations according to qualifications, job authorization and established procedures.

Authority and approvals in neighboring roles | Authority in related and neighboring roles comes from enterprise authorization and construction, safety and professional standards. It usually does not include independent decisions on formulation or design changes, major fire prevention matters or their handling. Formulation or design changes, scaffold acceptance, specialized work and major rework should be referred to the appropriate roles or organizations.

Work authority | Stage supplies, mask and assist with surface preparation as assigned. Check task-specific safeguards, training and authorization for spraying, scaffolds, work at height and hazardous materials. Stop and report if the assignment is unclear.

Limits on conclusions in neighboring roles | Conclusions in related and neighboring roles are mostly limited to the relevant process or location and generally do not determine finish acceptance, fire safety or legal liability. Conclusions spanning specialties or involving fire prevention, chemicals or major safety issues have limits on their applicability.

Limits on conclusions in this occupation | Conclusions on mixing, surface preparation, masking, cleaning and curing should state only verifiable material quantities, work performed and results, distinguishing measured facts, judgments and inferences, and matters awaiting verification. Workers must not issue conclusions in their own name on matters beyond their qualifications, such as scaffold acceptance, fire prevention and chemical compliance determinations, or final project acceptance.

Checks before joining | Use the following six items when applying and before starting work, to avoid inferring actual duties and authority from job titles or promotional wording. Base findings on written recruitment information, employment contracts, job descriptions, and construction and safety procedures, and keep confirming them after joining. This page lists checks only and does not constitute a hiring or safety determination.

Check guidance | Similar job titles may have very different duties and authority. Some focus on materials, mixing and cleaning; others on surface preparation, masking and application assistance; others on particular locations, such as interior painting, exterior walls, plastering or paperhanging; and some also involve scaffolding, spraying or assistance at height. Chemical, specialized work, qualification and safety requirements vary by enterprise and jurisdiction. Check these before assessing fit.

01 Actual duties, work and site authority | Check whether the role actually performs site work involving materials, mixing, surface preparation, masking and application assistance, or mainly handling, cleaning and support. Confirm permitted project types and locations, such as interiors, exterior walls, plastering or paperhanging; authority to use tools, equipment and spraying equipment; authorization to participate in scaffolding, work at height and chemical work; and interfaces with skilled workers, crews, materials personnel and safety personnel.

Job checklist | Exposure to sanding dust, material odors, noise, heights or cramped areas depends on the process, materials, equipment and site. Ask about the actual work area, safeguards, supervision and which equipment you can use. For scaffold, spray or other tasks subject to special rules, check the requirements for training, qualifications and authorization.

02 Safety, occupational health, chemical, height and machinery requirements | Check whether the employer requires and provides safe operating procedures and training for scaffolding, work at height and open edges; safe use, ventilation and fire prevention requirements for chemicals, paint and solvents; personal protection, emergency response and drills; handling and reporting requirements for solvent and paint residues, waste, dust and noise; and requirements to identify and report site and chemical hazards.

Check guidance | U.S. O*NET places 47-3014.00, Helpers--Painters, Paperhangers, Plasterers, and Stucco Masons, in Job Zone 1-2 (little or no preparation to some preparation needed), with an SVP range below 6.0 (SVP Below 6.0). The education section reports that 68% indicate less than a high school diploma is required, 26% a high school diploma or equivalent, and 4% a postsecondary certificate (the three categories listed on that page). In the U.S., preparation usually involves short-term on-the-job training. Check registered apprenticeships separately.

Entry preparation | BLS lists no formal educational credential and short-term on-the-job training as typical U.S. preparation. Ask the employer about supervision, permitted tasks and any optional apprenticeship route. Check the requirements for each regulated assignment.

Before accepting the job, ask about the work area. O*NET’s contaminants question does not isolate solvents. If the assignment uses solvent-based products, check the safety data sheet, ventilation and safeguards. Ask about standing, lifting and sanding.

04 Check pay and hours | Ask about base pay, the pay period, shifts, overtime, work location and employment terms. Ask about benefits and training that apply at that site. The national wage percentiles describe the U.S. market.

Check guidance | Interfaces with skilled workers, crews, project teams, materials suppliers and safety personnel determine the boundaries of mixing, surface preparation, application, acceptance, authority, responsibility and disclosure, and must be clarified beforehand.

05 Interfaces with skilled workers, crews and project teams | Confirm authority to approve and adjust materials, mix ratios and quantities; arrangements for requesting, using and reviewing tools, equipment and spraying equipment; processes for surface preparation, masking, application, nonconformities and rework; and requirements for handling and externally providing project and supplier technical information.

Check guidance | Traceability and recordkeeping requirements for work orders, materials, mixing, quantities, surface preparation, cleaning, curing and abnormalities determine quality and responsibility boundaries. Clarify templates, deadlines, amendment, archiving, access and retention rules beforehand. Project and supplier technical information must also be managed according to confidentiality and minimum-necessary requirements.

06 Materials, surfaces, cleanup and record requirements | Check requirements for work order records; materials, mix ratios and quantities; surface preparation, sanding and dust removal; masking and protection; painting, plastering or paperhanging and curing; cleaning and restoration; abnormalities, rework and outstanding items; and work permits, shift handovers, original records and revision trails.
